details:
It's no surprise to anyone who has been to Performance Gated instances that better performing avatars most often equals better performance for you as a VRChat user. However, most avatar creators do not have the skill and/or want to bring their avatar down to Poor or better rank. Poor or better avatars (especially in the extremely restrictive Android platform rankings) can be extremely challenging to make while still retaining the shape of the original clothes and the original detail (in polygons) or a very flowy look for dancing (in physbones) which was sought after on the avatar. While many optimizations nowadays can be made easily in Unity with some useful packages, polygon reduction on especially very heavy avatars remains an issue and requires learning the additional program Blender.

Furthermore, Android/Standalone users are really losing out on experiences in performance gated instances. Avatar creators who struggle enough to get their avatar to the "poor or better" rank often only edit and optimize the Android avatars enough to make them look the same as the PC counterpart and to be under the Android limits for upload. Often, many of these "optimized on PC, converted to Android" avatars are quite optimized on both platforms BUT they are still very poor rank and far above the limits to be able to be seen in performance gated instances by Android users. 

While PC users are reaping the benefits of performance gating (in the form of... well, better performance), Android/Quest standalone users who visit performance gated instances have told me that they cannot see their friend's avatars which were painstakingly converted to Android. Avatar performance overrides often have to be used heavily for the Android users to see any avatars at all. Furthermore, Performance Gating overall discourages PC users and Android users alike to use a poor or better avatar on Android. Simply put, many VRChat users value realism that is not able to be achieved in 20k polygons so they would rather avoid creating an Android version of their avatar all together if they are a PC user.

Additionally, many events of many different kinds struggle with allowing Very Poor with a "limit"... only for their attendees to not heed these limits and cause the performers and other attendees to lag and crash anyways. Common imposed limits in some communities look like the ask for "no realtime lights", "no more than 300 texture memory", "no more than 500,000 polygons", etc. Very few computers can also record events of entirely "very poor" rank users nowadays as the average "very poor" avatar has gotten heavier and larger memory. Due to the ranking system being so absolute, an avatar which is "good" on all regards other than one metric gets tanked into the "very poor" rank, even if it does not cause performance issues. 

At the same time, the average PC is more powerful than it was even 3 years ago. At this moment, a full instance which has mostly poor or better avatars and a few performance-overridden more optimized very poor avatars can also easily be recorded on an even a few generation old PC. 

With the needs of the community and the want for inclusivity in mind, I propose one simple additional rank called "Extremely Poor".

Very Poor rank could look like up to this on PC: 

Up to 99,999 polygons

A few more physbones

Up to 200mb texture memory

Up to 40 material slots

Up to 10 trail renders

More total cloth vertices

Etc

Very Poor rank could look like up to this rank on Android/iOS:

Up to 69,999 polygons

Up to 12 material slots

Up to 4 skinned meshes

The maximum amount of current components that do not cause as much performance impact

Etc

Any avatars which exceed the above limits could then be categorized into a very much not wanted rank called "Extremely Poor". A lot of events which have many Android users or many higher end PC users with highly custom avatars or even events which are predicting less attendance could instead set the instance to an easier to attain "Very Poor" avatar rank for the "Very Poor or better" performance gate. I suspect that many events which do not currently use any performance gating would swap to "Very Poor" or better with limits like these as they are more in line with what they want (some restrictions but not as strict as poor or better.) I also suspect that groups which use "Poor or better" performance gated instances would continue to do so or experiment with this new rank. This could also encourage users to Android convert more of their content as they only would have to optimize their "good on PC" avatar a little more to get it to "very poor" on Android.

Additionally, the implementation of this rank could go hand-in-hand with other updates and warnings in the SDK or in client to increase overall VRChat performance in instances. 

As a final note on this, VRChat does not have to endorse using such performance gated instances. This would simply give the users more creative freedom which still maintaining SOME semblance of optimization in instances. VRChat probably would benefit from less extremely large file size avatars being uploaded to the platform overall due to server costs. However, eliminating these very heavy "extremely poor" avatars is also not a solution as VRChat has a long history of avatar showcases and particle shows which need the avatars to be large in size and full featured.

Thank you for reading and I hope you will think about and consider this proposal.
title: A Proposed Addition to the Avatar Ranking System: "Extremely Poor" Rank
